transit: trānseō, -īre, -iī, -itum — to go through, pass through, pierce (3rd sg. pres. ind. act.)
transverberat: trānsverberō, -āre — to pierce through, transfix (3rd sg. pres.)
tum: tum (adv.) — then, at that time; next
uncis: uncus, -a, -um — hooked, curved, crooked (m./f./n. abl. pl.)
unum: ūnus, -a, -um — one, a single, the same (n. nom./acc. sg.; m. acc. sg.)
ventosa: ventōsus, -a, -um — windy, stormy, wind-swept (n. acc. pl.; ventōsa aequora) · also f. abl. sg. (ventōsā in linguā)
versare: versō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to turn over, turn about, ply, contrive (pres. inf.)
versat: versō, -āre — to turn over, ponder (3rd sg. pres.)
verso: vertō, -ere, vertī, versum — to turn, turn round (perf. pass. part., m. abl. sg.)
vertice: vertex, verticis (m.) — peak, summit; whirl (abl. sg.)
vertitur: vertō, vertere, vertī, versum — to turn; vertitur, wheels round (3rd sg. pres. pass.)
vestra: vester, vestra, vestrum — your (pl.) (f. nom. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.)
viri: vir, virī (m.) — man, hero, husband (nom. pl.; gen. sg.) · also voc. pl. (festīnāte, virī)
viro: vir, virī (m.) — man (dat. sg.) · also abl. sg. (proque virō, in place of the man)
vomens: vomō, -ere, -uī, -itum — to vomit, belch forth, pour out (pres. part., m./f./n. nom. sg.)
vulnus: vulnus, vulneris (n.) (= volnus) — wound, blow (nom./acc. sg.)
